blocks.x: Data & Lakehouse inside Reinsurance & Commercial Lines: the operating realities we design for, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

Reinsurance and specialty commercial books trade in complexity: treaty structures, cat exposure, bordereaux reconciliation and capital optimization. The data flows between cedants, reinsurers and brokers are still largely spreadsheets — which is why settlement cycles and model confidence suffer.

items: Ceded premium/loss bordereaux arrive in formats and qualities; reconciliation consumes analysts and hides data quality issues.
Retro programs and cat capacity buying are combinatorial; incumbent methods stop early.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Data Monetization & Analytics Products, Advanced Risk & Predictive Analytics, Lakehouse Architecture & Migration from the Data, Analytics & Lakehouse tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Bordereaux intake/reconciliation, Treaty settlement, Retro/capacity optimization) on Dataq Forge and Dataq Nexus. Governance inherits the sector frame — Solvency II / RBC among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Lakehouse the right way: Unity Catalog governance, cost-aware design and AI-ready foundations.
Decisions at event speed: sub-second pipelines from sensor, click or transaction to action.
Metrics into management: one governed semantic layer, decision cadence built in.
Format-normalized intake with auto-reconciliation and quality scoring (70%+ auto-reconciled)

At Insurance & Risk level this capability reads as: triangle pipelines, chain-ladder and ML hybrids with actuarial-in-command controls (reserve review cycles shortened materially). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

Programs run on the fixed rhythm below, chosen so progress is legible from week one. Weeks 1–2 are measurement only: we lock the current metric with your team and both sides sign it before a line of build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver a bounded pilot — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a named control owner on your side. Weeks 9–12 turn what worked into runbooks, monitoring and enablement, then report the measured delta against the baseline. A missed gate means a documented stop-or-redirect decision, not a quiet extension.
